column4: Identical camera and cathedral aisle as the first reference, looking toward the exit doors. The living librarian (second reference) walks away from the viewer down the center of the aisle, seen from behind, her long orange hair down her back. In the pews on both sides, coal-hooded congregants sit hunched over ledgers, faces hidden. No strings, no text.

Identical overhead ledger on the pew rail as the first reference, the open pages now filled with rows of orange tally marks and checkboxes; a pair of coal-black hooded sleeves with pale hands holds both covers, about to close it. No text lettering.

Same layout as the first reference: on the left the living librarian (second reference) seen from behind over her shoulder, long orange hair, white blouse; on the right inside the tall mirror frame, a brand-new porcelain maid doll (third reference) with eyes now open, standing face to face with her, the same face. Ball joints and wrist ring only on the doll. No text.

Low view from behind the living librarian (second reference) standing before the tall stained-glass icon window of the first reference, which towers over her. She raises the large black dressmaker shears high above her head in both hands, blades closed like a dagger, ready to strike the glass. No text.

Close-up of the stained-glass icon window (first reference): the point of large black dressmaker shears has struck the glass at the icon's chest; a star of sharp straight cracks radiates out across the leaded panes. Only the shears tip and the glass. No text.
